about: The contract for ~/.config/biopb/extra-packages.txt: file content in, the
requirement list the installer passes to `uv tool install --with` out.
There are TWO implementations of this parser -- install.sh's
independently for bash and PowerShell. Both had the same bug (biopb/biopb#648:
a `#` anywhere ended the line, so a PEP 508 direct reference lost its URL
fragment and silently installed something else). Nothing made them agree.
This file is what makes them agree. test_extras_contract.py runs EVERY case
below through BOTH parsers, so the two cannot drift without a test failing.
Add a case here, not to one suite -- a case added to only one parser's tests
is exactly the hole this exists to close.
The comment rule is pip's, from requirements.txt: `#` starts a comment only at
line start or after whitespace. Everywhere else it is data.

cases.why: The ordinary case: one bare requirement.
A pinned requirement passes through with its specifier intact.
One requirement per line, order preserved.
An empty file means no extras, not an empty requirement.
Blank and whitespace-only lines are skipped, not passed to uv as ''.
A `#` at line start comments out the whole line.
Leading whitespace before the `#` still makes it a full-line comment.
cases.input:
# temporarily disabled
        # and this one
basicpy

cases.why: `#basicpy` is a commented-out line, not a package named '#basicpy'. The rule is about what precedes the `#`, not what follows it.
A `#` after whitespace ends the requirement; the note is not part of it.
Any whitespace counts, not just a space.
An empty comment leaves the requirement and takes the separating space with it.

THE MOTIVATING BUG (#648). `#subdirectory=` is a PEP 508 URL fragment with no whitespace before it, so it is data. Truncating here does not fail -- uv installs the repo ROOT under the right name, and the user gets a different package with nothing to warn about.
Same shape, worse consequence: dropping `#sha256=` silently disables the hash check on a directly-referenced wheel.
The legacy `#egg=` fragment names the package a VCS URL provides; without it the requirement can fail to resolve at all.

Both rules on one line at once: the fragment is kept (no whitespace before its `#`) and the trailing comment is stripped (whitespace before its `#`). A parser that decides per LINE which `#` to honour, rather than per occurrence, has to pick one and gets the other wrong.
Indentation and trailing spaces are not part of the requirement.
The file is the user's, and on Windows -- where the GUI installer runs -- their editor writes CRLF. A retained \r rides along into the requirement string and makes uv reject it.
The \r must go even when the comment strip already ran.
A file whose last line lacks a newline -- what an editor that does not add one leaves behind. The last requirement must not be dropped.
Full PEP 508 syntax -- extras in brackets, an environment marker after a semicolon -- survives intact, including the spaces inside it.
A local version segment carries a '+'. Nothing in the comment strip may touch it.
The realistic file: a header comment, real requirements, a disabled line, a fragment, and a note.
